key_idea: If a<b, let d be the highest bit where they differ and P the common prefix: the range contains both P 0 1^d and P 1 0^d, forcing popcount(P)+d+1 coins, which is achieved by the bits of P plus coins 2^0..2^d.
sketch: Pad a with leading zeros to the length of b and scan for the first differing position. If a == b the answer is popcount(a) (binary representation is the unique minimum-coin payment). Otherwise the answer is popcount(common prefix) + (number of bits from the first differing position to the end). Lower bound: paying P01..1 needs at least popcount(P)+d coins, and with exactly that many the coin set is forced to be its binary representation whose total is below P10..0, so one more coin is required. Upper bound: prefix bits plus one coin of each 2^0..2^d pays every value P*2^(d+1)+[0,2^(d+1)-1]. O(length) on up to 1e6 bits; read as strings. Verified against exhaustive multiset search for all 1 <= a <= b < 40.
